claims.head: Depth vs. star power
claims.body: On depth, the Islanders are the league’s best, but Columbus is near the bottom. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Islanders.

NYI.head: Leaning the Islanders’ way
NYI.body: The Islanders have home-ice advantage, but Columbus has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Blue Jackets can still swing it if they get good looks.

CBJ.head: A slightly uphill night for the Blue Jackets
CBJ.body: The Islanders have home-ice advantage, but Columbus has been out-chancing opponents lately. The Blue Jackets can tip it if they get good looks.

story.head: The Blue Jackets are searching for answers
paras: The Islanders have won two in a row, the last a 6-2 rout of Anaheim. The Blue Jackets are on a four-game losing streak. This is a Metropolitan Division matchup, with the Jackets last (29th in the NHL) and the Islanders fourth (tied for 18th).

The Blue Jackets have played better than their record (.389) says: their chances are worth about .495, and their finishing has held them back. The Islanders’ record (.579) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.476), largely thanks to their goaltending. If their records matched their chances, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Islanders (1st) and the Blue Jackets (3rd) both get their defensemen shooting. The Blue Jackets do a lot of their shooting from distance (4th lowest). They also forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd), and that could keep the Islanders pinned in their own end. Columbus has scored 2.39 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. On the other side, the Islanders have had the league’s best goaltending (1st). They also roll their lines more evenly than anyone (1st), so the Islanders roll four lines, but the Blue Jackets lean on their top six.

Kent Johnson (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 18 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, and Zach Werenski (2 G / 13 A / 15 P in 18 GP) is next in line. For the Islanders, Matthew Schaefer (6 G / 15 A / 21 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Bo Horvat (9 G / 11 A / 20 P in 19 GP) has a team-high nine goals, with seven goals in eleven games against Columbus since 2023-24.
Cam Talbot (5-3-0 / .907 SV% in 8 GS) is expected to go for Columbus. Ilya Sorokin (7-4-2 / .915 SV% in 13 GS) has been outstanding for the Islanders and is expected to start.
